children: Germany's SEFE, a gas importer under government control, said on Wednesday it had independently decided to increase natural gas storage and had not been ordered by the German economy ministry to do so.
"SEFE ...has taken an independent commercial decision to fill the booked storage capacity," said the company, which also operates gas pipelines and storage facilities in Germany.

A government source told Reuters earlier on Wednesday that Economy Minister Katherina Reiche would use market incentives to shore up gas storage for winter heating, while avoiding direct state purchases.
The government has also agreed with state-owned energy companies Uniper
and SEFE that they will make fuller use of their storage capabilities, the source added, following growing concerns over low inventories.
Germany's gas storage sites were around 53% full in early September, the lowest level for the time of year since records began 15 years ago, according to storage association INES.
